claims.claim: NorMuon combines Muon's orthogonalized updates with neuron-wise adaptive normalization based on second-order momentum statistics (Algorithm 1).
claims.evidence: The pinned official normuon.py update matches an independently implemented Algorithm 1 reference on deterministic synthetic gradients.

claims.claim: The optimizer analysis shows Muon lowers update condition numbers but leaves high variance in per-neuron update norms, while NorMuon normalizes neuron contributions (Figure 1).
claims.evidence: A CPU synthetic update with deliberately uneven row norms shows the NorMuon adaptive normalization step reduces row-norm dispersion while restoring total update norm.

claims.claim: NorMuon achieves 21.74% better step efficiency than Adam and 11.31% improvement over Muon on the 1.1B pretraining setting (Table 1).
claims.evidence: Not reproduced: this claim requires GPU-scale LLM pretraining or large model benchmark runs outside the CPU-only budget.

claims.claim: NorMuon also improves validation-loss trajectories over Muon and AdamW at the 5.4B scale (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: Not reproduced: this claim requires GPU-scale LLM pretraining or large model benchmark runs outside the CPU-only budget.

claims.claim: On 5.4B training, NorMuon keeps optimizer-state memory close to Muon and below AdamW, with about 2.9% total training-step time overhead over AdamW (Table 2).
claims.evidence: Not reproduced: this claim requires GPU-scale LLM pretraining or large model benchmark runs outside the CPU-only budget.

claims.claim: NorMuon outperforms Muon in Modded-NanoGPT pretraining at 124M and 350M parameter scales (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: Not reproduced: this claim requires GPU-scale LLM pretraining or large model benchmark runs outside the CPU-only budget.

limitations: GPU-scale LLM pretraining efficiency, 5.4B validation loss, memory, and Modded-NanoGPT claims were not reproduced.
The mechanism tests use deterministic CPU synthetic gradients and do not claim paper-scale training performance.
